item.title: Multiple arrests on suspicion of explosives offenses near U.K. base used by U.S. forces
item.description: Police evacuated homes Sunday near an air base in England used by the U.S. and arrested several men over suspected explosives offenses.

item.title: These Democrats are running for Congress on Christian faith. Will it pay off?
item.description: It's rare for Democrats to make religion a centerpiece of their campaigns. But this midterm election cycle, a number of candidates for Congress are doing just that.

item.title: Trump gave Xi Jinping a warm welcome. What did the talks accomplish?
item.description: From the National Archives to the state dinner, President Trump and Xi Jinping looked comfortable together in Washington. Two former NPR China correspondents on what the visit did and didn't deliver.

item.title: Trump calls Iranian plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz not 'acceptable'
item.description: President Trump said he was rejecting an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian proposal is similar to a memorandum of understanding agreed upon by the U.S. and Iran back in June.

item.title: OPINION: Trump's U.N. speech, a stark contrast with past presidents
item.description: President Donald Trump mused openly before the United Nations about whether he should annihilate Iran. It's a stark contrast to how his predecessors have spoken about wielding US military power.

item.title: Why this island paradise has the world's fastest-growing HIV epidemic
item.description: In mid-September, Fiji's government declared a national emergency because of a startling rise in HIV infections. The country's crystal meth epidemic is a strong contributing factor.

item.title: Meal deliveries can save money and improve health. Will they survive Medicaid cuts?
item.description: Some states deliver meals to Medicaid patients that address their dietary needs. Evidence shows it aids recovery and saves healthcare costs, but federal budget cuts may lead some states to cancel it.
